_readme: Curated one-line blurbs for the poster headline block, keyed by year. KRISHNA CAN EDIT THIS FILE FREELY. Rules: a complete sentence, max 140 characters, no abbreviations that need context. Years with no entry show only the headline stat (never a truncated event string). Run the build after editing so the file gets a fresh cache stamp.
1526: Babur's victory at Panipat ends the Delhi Sultanate and plants the Mughal dynasty in Hindustan.
1556: Fourteen-year-old Akbar and Bairam Khan defeat Hemu at Panipat, securing the Mughal restoration.
1565: Talikota shatters Vijayanagara; the last great empire of the south never recovers.
1600: Akbar's empire spans Hindustan as a London charter quietly births the East India Company.
1658: Aurangzeb takes the throne from Shah Jahan; the empire reaches for the whole subcontinent.
1680: Shivaji dies at Raigad, leaving a Maratha state strong enough to outlast Aurangzeb's onslaught.
1700: Aurangzeb's empire stands at its widest, yet the long Deccan wars are hollowing it from within.
1707: Aurangzeb dies at Ahmednagar; three sons contest the throne and the great decline begins.
1724: Nizam-ul-Mulk withdraws to the Deccan and founds the Hyderabad state in all but name.
1739: Nadir Shah sacks Delhi and carries off the Peacock Throne; Mughal prestige never recovers.
1757: Plassey delivers Bengal's revenues to the East India Company — an empire begun by accountants.
1760: The Marathas stand at their zenith, masters of more of India than anyone since the great Mughals.
1761: At Panipat the Durranis break the Maratha army; a generation of commanders falls in one afternoon.
1764: Buxar seals what Plassey began: the Company becomes the real power on the lower Ganga.
1799: Tipu Sultan dies in the breach at Seringapatam; Mysore falls and the road south lies open.
1818: The Third Anglo-Maratha War ends; the Company stands paramount from the Indus to Bengal.
1849: The Sikh Empire, last great Indian power standing, is annexed after Gujrat.
1857: The great uprising sweeps northern India before it is crushed; Company rule has a year to live.
1858: The Crown takes India from the Company; the Raj begins with Queen Victoria's proclamation.
1905: Curzon partitions Bengal and ignites Swadeshi — the first truly mass politics of the freedom struggle.
1911: At the Coronation Durbar the capital moves from Calcutta to Delhi.
1930: Gandhi walks to Dandi and lifts a handful of salt; civil disobedience sweeps the land.
1947: At midnight, freedom — and Partition: two nations are born and a million lives are uprooted.
1971: Bangladesh is born from war in the east; the map of 1947 is redrawn once more.
2026: The subcontinent today — three republics, one shared history, on a single district-level map.
